comparator.name: Political Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated English curriculum totals sixty EC per year. International Relations is retained using the first-listed specialisation on the primary programme page. The twelve-credit core module, six-credit sustainability elective, eighteen seminar credits, twelve-credit thesis project and thirty open credits form one route; other specialisations are not added to its total.
components: History of Europe and the modern world since 1750
Academic skills for political scientists I
Academic skills for political scientists II
Academic skills for political scientists III
Research Methods requires at least 42 first-year EC, including Introduction to Political Science Research. The later research project requires Research Methods; this pathway completes it first.
Research project II: Practicing research skills
The International Relations core module requires at least 42 first-year EC. This example retains the specialisation selected from the primary programme page before UCR construction.

This example selects Sustainability Politics: Perspectives and Debates, 6 EC. It requires at least 42 first-year EC and cannot be combined with the alternative Violence and Security or European Union Politics module.

Beyond the Headlines is an eligible 6 EC seminar in the International Relations route. The 2026–2027 offering examines American politics and its international connections. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC.

Democratic Backsliding is an eligible 12 EC seminar in the International Relations route. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC; prior Democracies, Autocracies and Transitions is recommended.

The selected 12 EC thesis project is Contesting the Liberal International Order. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC, including Research Methods. Completing both prior years meets the condition. The selected seminars and thesis are offered in the first semester; thirty EC remain open afterward.
Thirty EC remain open for approved elective or minor study within or outside Political Science, exchange or an optional placement. No particular minor, placement host or elective is assumed.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor has five official core-module specialisations and none is identified as the broad default. International Relations is listed first in the current official curriculum, so it is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break before and independently of UCR course selection.

core: Political power, institutions, democracy, authoritarianism and decision-making
International relations, conflict, cooperation, security and global governance
Public policy, governance, political economy and government responses to social problems
Political inequality, identity and the relationship between politics and society
Qualitative, quantitative and comparative political research and independent inquiry
adjacent: Political theory, rights, law and the ethics of globalisation
European and regional politics, institutions and foreign policy
questions: How do democratic and authoritarian institutions organise power and representation?
Why do political actors conflict or cooperate across states and global institutions?
How can governments design and evaluate policy responses to inequality and global challenges?

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
trace: develops academic writing, civic collaboration and reflective professional practice
introduces economic reasoning about markets, resources and government as a foundation for political-economic analysis
examines open-economy macroeconomic dynamics, goods, financial and labour markets, inflation, growth, and fiscal and monetary policy using formal models
examines microeconomic decisions, incentives and behavioural responses, supporting analysis of policy effects and political-economic choices
examines public intervention, equity, public goods, taxation, education, health and social insurance through policy models and research
develops econometric estimation, statistical tests and an empirical paper for analysing causal and predictive economic relationships relevant to policy
develops empirical design, measurement, sampling, statistics and a complete student data-collection project as research foundations for political inquiry
develops data cleaning, transformation, visualisation and applied research in R, supporting empirical investigation of political evidence
develops statistical prediction, regression, classification, model evaluation and data analysis as computational complements to political research
examines institutions, power, participation, justice and collective decision-making in sustainability governance, including a policy-advice or evaluation project
introduces legal traditions, social justice and legal reasoning as foundations for studying political institutions and public power
examines modern political, economic and cultural transformations from 1815 onward through historical sources and inquiry
compares ancient and modern empires through legitimacy, institutions and cultural power, providing historical depth for international politics
examines warfare, strategy and political power from antiquity onward through historical sources and critical comparison
develops research questions, source criticism and a substantial historical research paper in the American context; its contribution is historical inquiry rather than a current US-politics survey
examines human-rights law and philosophical claims, dignity, international protection and legal-political arguments

examines criminal liability, punishment, criminalisation and justice through legal cases and a criminology or organised-crime research proposal; it adds a legal perspective on security rather than replacing international-relations theory
examines international legal sources, states and institutions, force, conflict, human rights, economic and environmental law, and the political dimensions of law
compares constitutions, legislatures, executives, courts, judicial review, rights and administrative remedies as structures of public power
examines EU institutions, competences, supremacy, citizenship, free movement and judicial remedies through legal cases
develops interpretation and evaluation of philosophical arguments about ethics, knowledge, freedom and identity as foundations for normative political thought
develops moral reasoning and independent ethical arguments relevant to public responsibilities and competing political values
examines historical and contemporary political thought, authority, rights and society through original texts and normative argument
examines democracy, autocratisation, institutions, participation and political behaviour through empirical comparison and a research memo
examines competing international-relations theories, geopolitics, conflicts and global cooperation through case research and a UN simulation
examines EU institutions, integration, representation, legitimacy and policymaking, with an empirical research project on parliamentary amendments and interest influence
examines policy-making phases, policy actors and alternative analytical frameworks through a sugar-policy case and policy memos
examines conflict, inequality, identity and colonial legacies through interdisciplinary approaches to security, peacebuilding and justice, including a policy brief
examines social identities, institutions, boundaries and inequality as contexts for political participation and power
develops qualitative interviewing, documentary inquiry, interpretation and reflexivity for social and political research
examines competing modern social theories of power, inequality and cultural difference through critical reading and an empirical case paper
examines social movements, environmental justice and collective action through feminist, anticolonial and other perspectives
examines civil society, trust, solidarity, hegemony and social repair through theory and research on an organisation or initiative
examines social influence, group processes, prejudice, aggression and prosocial behaviour as psychological foundations for political interaction
examines youth radicalisation, risk, belonging, inclusive education and prevention through research-based teacher resources and a youth toolkit
develops rhetorical argument, audience awareness and public communication as complementary foundations for political debate
examines persuasion, framing and ethical communication through community projects, supporting critical analysis of public communication

alternatives.label: Political institutions, democracy & social change
alternatives.concept: Study power, institutions, democracy and social change through comparative politics, political philosophy and international relations. Combine modern history, law, social theory, research and public-policy analysis with sustainability governance.
alternatives.labelReason: Study power, institutions, democracy and social change through comparative politics, political philosophy and international relations. Combine modern history, law, social theory, research and public-policy analysis with sustainability governance.
progression: Checked every current offered term and earlier formal prerequisite. Comparative-politics foundations precede policy analysis, introductory sociology precedes advanced social theory where selected, and data foundations precede machine learning.

alternatives.label: International relations, conflict & global governance
alternatives.concept: Study international relations and conflict through political theory, international and EU law, histories of empire and war, peacebuilding and public policy. Social psychology, youth resilience and criminal justice add bounded perspectives on social conflict and security.
alternatives.labelReason: Study international relations and conflict through political theory, international and EU law, histories of empire and war, peacebuilding and public policy. Social psychology, youth resilience and criminal justice add bounded perspectives on social conflict and security.
alternatives.distinctness: This option gives more weight to empire, warfare, peacebuilding, rights, criminal justice and youth prevention. The closest option balances domestic institutions, constitutional comparison, modern history and social theory.
progression: Checked every current offered term and earlier formal prerequisite. Comparative-politics foundations precede policy analysis, introductory sociology precedes advanced social theory where selected, and data foundations precede machine learning.

alternatives.label: Public policy, political economy & governance
alternatives.concept: Study public policy and political economy through political institutions, economics, law and empirical research. Combine public spending and distribution, international macroeconomics, behavioural economics, econometrics and data analysis with historical and qualitative inquiry.
alternatives.labelReason: Study public policy and political economy through political institutions, economics, law and empirical research. Combine public spending and distribution, international macroeconomics, behavioural economics, econometrics and data analysis with historical and qualitative inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: This option gives sustained weight to public and international economics, behavioural decisions, econometrics and computational methods alongside political and legal institutions. The other options devote more space to social theory or international conflict.
progression: Checked every current offered term and earlier formal prerequisite. Comparative-politics foundations precede policy analysis, introductory sociology precedes advanced social theory where selected, and data foundations precede machine learning.

selection.assessment: A broad political-institutions response is the closest option. International conflict/governance and policy/political economy are separately evidenced priorities with concrete curricular consequences. Each pair exceeds thirty EC and has a substantively different emphasis. Three is the maximum.

blocks: Both examine government policy in relation to economic organisation and distribution. UvA also studies the history and institutional foundations of capitalism and political-economic theory; UCR concentrates on public intervention and spending.
Both develop research design, evidence evaluation, measurement and empirical analysis. UCR includes a student research project in a broader disciplinary setting.
Both examine sustainability transitions through power, institutions, inclusion, collective action and governance frameworks.
Both study the historical development of modern political, economic and social systems. UCR starts in 1815 rather than 1750.
Both develop an independent academic research question, source work and a substantial scholarly paper. UCR uses historical rather than specifically political-science inquiry.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, rights and legal constraints on public power. UvA situates these in an integrated law-and-politics introduction.
Both examine the history of political ideas through primary texts and relate them to political problems.
Both compare democratic and authoritarian institutions, transitions, political actors and explanations of regime change.
Both develop international-relations theories and apply them to global political problems.
Both develop a political research design, collect or code evidence and analyse and communicate findings. UCR uses an EU parliamentary project; UvA offers broader supervised research themes.
Both examine public policy, actors, policy processes and frameworks for analysing collective responses to social problems.

Both examine international power, conflict, colonial legacies, inequality and security. UvA is a broader advanced survey of International Relations; UCR concentrates on conflict and peace through several disciplines.
Both develop empirical inquiry and methodological judgement. UCR specialises in qualitative methods; UvA also includes quantitative and inferential statistical methods.
Both analyse power, inequality, social categories and difference through competing theoretical perspectives. UvA gives a specifically political and intersectional focus.
No additional selected course directly reproduces the dedicated political-science academic-skills sequence.
Selected political courses address parts of this broad introduction, but their strongest placements are political thought, international relations and comparative regimes. They are not counted twice.
UCR research and political projects are placed with methods and the later research project; no additional course is counted as the distinct first-year project.
No additional selected course directly reproduces the dedicated political-science academic-skills sequence.
No additional selected course directly centres the seminar’s current American-politics and international-connections focus.
Comparative Politics already supplies its strongest primary relationship with the compulsory regimes course. No second course is counted for the specialist backsliding seminar.
No compulsory individual political-science thesis is scheduled at UCR. Optional research is shown separately outside scheduled credits.
Open choice space remains unspecified; no elective, minor or placement is invented.

notes.text: UvA provides a dedicated Political Science sequence with a chosen core module, advanced seminars, integrated research training and a required thesis. The UCR options combine substantial political study with law, history, social theory, economics and methods. The comparison shows partial academic relationships rather than equivalent specialist sequences.

audience.programmeDescription: Political Science at UvA studies power, institutions, political ideas, international relations and public policy through social-scientific research. Students complete a specialisation, advanced seminars and a thesis. This example uses International Relations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can combine substantial political study with history, law, social theory, economics and methods. Its options prioritise political institutions and social change, international conflict and governance, or policy and political economy. UvA provides a more integrated specialist and research sequence.
